title: Which rangoli rectangle needs more powder?
description: Two rectangles, seven by four and eight by three, are packed with unit squares and the squares are counted in each. Seven times four and eight times three show which rectangle covers more. Keeko doubts this and says the longer rectangle must need more powder.
teaching_notes: One idea: area is the number of unit squares that fit, so length times width gives it. Watch for children who think the longer rectangle must cover more.

source: A rangoli artist has a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle and an 8 cm by
video_script.why: The child sees that area, not length, decides how much powder a region needs, and that counting unit squares gives length times width.
video_script.substitution: Pack unit squares into each rectangle, count them with length times width, and compare the two counts.
video_script.anchor: the two rectangles of the book that are coloured with rangoli powder
video_script.wrong_answer: the eight centimetre one needs more powder
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the rectangle with the longer side. It is longer but thinner, and counting unit squares shows it holds fewer.
video_script.payoff_line: the seven by four rectangle needs more powder

final_answer.value: 7 cm by 4 cm needs more powder: 28 cm² against 24 cm²
final_answer.spoken: twenty eight square centimetres against twenty four

hold_back: the 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle needs more powder
never_show: which rectangle needs more powder, before the answer beat
maths_rules: first rectangle 7 cm by 4 cm: 7 rows of 4 unit squares; 7 × 4 = 28; area 28 cm²
second rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm: 8 rows of 3 unit squares; 8 × 3 = 24; area 24 cm²
28 > 24, so the 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle needs more powder
a unit square has sides 1 cm and area 1 cm²; area of a rectangle = length × width
video_script.design: One idea: count unit squares, which is length times width. Wrong idea: the longer rectangle needs more. The two rectangles stay on stage from the hook to the end; the working lines stack on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the eight centimetre one needs more powder, because it is longer.
<bookmark mark='thin'/>But it is only three centimetres wide, so it is thinner.
